notes: Reserved for the York/GBS DPI clip. Defender contacts and restricts receiver before the ball arrives. Common confusion: not holding because the ball is in flight and the receiver is attempting to catch a forward pass.

DPI category: early_contact. Obvious early contact before the ball arrives; defender materially restricts receiver before the pass gets there. Common confusion: not holding because the pass is in flight and the receiver is attempting to catch a forward pass.

DPI category: arm_bar/body_restrict. Borderline DPI. Defender restricts the receiver before the ball arrives on a catchable pass. Common confusion: incidental hand fighting versus restriction that affects the catch opportunity.
No foul. This should not be ruled pass interference. Common confusion: do not call DPI unless the defender materially restricts the receiver before the ball arrives and affects the catch opportunity.
Borderline DPI with catchable pass and early contact. Common confusion: no foul if the model overweights minor ball tracking and misses the timing of contact.
Obvious OPI. Receiver extends arm and pushes defender to create separation before the pass is touched. Common confusion: not DPI because the offensive player initiates the restriction.
Borderline OPI. Offensive player initiates contact on a route beyond the neutral zone to free a teammate. Common confusion: legal rub route if contact is incidental or within legal timing.
Offensive player blocks defender more than 1 yard downfield before a forward pass is touched. Common confusion: not holding because the issue is offensive pass interference timing.
Borderline OPI. Receiver creates late separation with meaningful contact before the ball arrives. Common confusion: normal route contact if the push does not materially affect the defender.

Obvious OPI. Offensive screen or pick prevents defender from covering the intended receiver before the pass is touched. Common confusion: legal blocking only after the pass is caught or restrictions no longer apply.
Obvious holding at or near the line of scrimmage. Blocker restrains defender outside the frame of the body. Common confusion: not a legal block if restriction changes the defender's path.
Borderline holding on edge pressure. Blocker grabs or hooks as defender attempts to disengage. Common confusion: legal hand placement versus visible restriction.
Holding affects the point of attack. Blocker restricts defender who is pursuing the runner. Common confusion: not ignored as away from the play if it affects the run lane.
Receiver or perimeter blocker restricts defender outside the frame. Common confusion: not OPI if the pass is not in flight to that receiver or it occurs during a run action.
Borderline holding. Jersey grab or arm hook turns the defender and prevents pursuit. Common confusion: momentary contact that does not restrict is not enough.
Clean coverage with defender playing the ball and only incidental contact. Common confusion: do not call DPI without material restriction before arrival.
Contact occurs on a pass that is clearly uncatchable or after the play is effectively over. Common confusion: do not call DPI when the receiver had no catch opportunity.
Legal block with hands inside the frame and no restriction. Common confusion: do not call holding just because the defender loses leverage.
Offense has fewer than seven players on the line at the snap or a clear numbering/alignment issue. Common confusion: not illegal motion because the foul is set alignment.
Borderline illegal motion. Player is moving forward at the snap or motion is not lateral/backward. Common confusion: legal motion if the player is not moving toward the opponent's goal line.
Players shift and fail to become set for the required interval before the snap. Common confusion: illegal motion involves movement at the snap; illegal shift involves failing to reset.
Obvious personal foul. Contact occurs after the runner is clearly out of bounds. Common confusion: not legal finishing contact when the player has time and space to avoid it.
Borderline personal foul for targeting or illegal helmet contact. Common confusion: not ordinary shoulder contact if the player initiates forcible contact to a protected area.
Horse-collar style tackle with grab and pull from behind or side. Common confusion: not legal tackle if the pull-down mechanism fits the rule.
Receiver is interfered with while attempting to catch a kick. Common confusion: not legal coverage if the receiver is denied an unimpeded opportunity.
Kicker is contacted after the kick when the defender could have avoided contact. Common confusion: distinguish roughing from running into based on severity and danger.
Free kick goes out of bounds untouched by the receiving team. Common confusion: not kick-catch interference because no receiver catch opportunity is involved.
